final_message:
Done. All 3 tests pass, plus I verified ~40 README edge cases (empty items, `5/2`, signs, spaces, decimals, unknown names, `A>B`, `S<1`, weekday `7→0` mapping, case-insensitive names).

Implementation in `cronfields/fields.py`:
- `expand_field` (cronfields/fields.py:9): splits on commas into a set (dedupes overlapping items), each item parsed by `_expand_item` → sorted list.
- `parse_cron` (cronfields/fields.py:18): splits on whitespace runs, requires exactly 5 fields, expands each with its range/names table; weekday `7` is remapped to `0` and deduped so `5-7` → `[0, 5, 6]`.
- Numbers (`N`, `A`, `B`) are range-checked; the step `S` is only required to be ≥ 1 (as the README states) — range-checking it would break e.g. `expand_field("*/1", 3, 5)`.
